title: Jewish Studies, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. New jst_catalog.json (JST 10) and hebr_catalog.json (HEBR 1/2/3, a coded prereq chain matching Spanish/German/Italian/Russian). 'JST/Related' (4 occurrences), '400-level HEBR', and '400-level JST/HEBR/Related' (4 occurrences) are modeled as generic slots, matching the bulletin's own open-range phrasing. 'LA 283' (the same unconfirmed code hit throughout recent Liberal Arts builds) replaced with a generic slot. This plan's computed 8-semester total (123cr) matches the bulletin's own stated total exactly. RE-VERIFIED against the live bulletin's full program-requirements PDF (2026-08): unlike several other Liberal Arts majors checked this session, Jewish Studies' 'Supporting Courses and Related Areas' (27cr, split as 3+3+3+18) is genuinely non-enumerable from any public source -- the bulletin itself defers every sub-category to 'approved program list or in consultation with the director,' a list the program does not publish externally. This plan's generic 'JST/Related Course' slots correctly reflect that real ambiguity; no fix needed there. Two real constraints were found that this plan doesn't yet enforce and are documented here for a future pass (same deferred-item precedent as CMPSC's grade-minimum tracking): (1) 'No more than 8 credits of Hebrew Language courses may count toward the requirements for the major' -- relevant if the generic 'JST/Related'/'400-level JST/HEBR/Related' slots are ever wired to recommend real courses, since several could resolve to HEBR. (2) 'No more than 15 credits in courses numbered 99, 199, 299, 399, or 499 may count toward the requirements for the major.' Both are unenforceable today only because the slots they'd apply to are still fully generic/unfilled placeholders, so neither is currently violated in practice.
